For an indirect system, connect collectors to a storage heat exchanger through a separate circulation loop with pump, expansion vessel and appropriate relief devices. Choose direct versus indirect circulation and pressurized versus other configurations only after reviewing climate, water quality, roof loading and local regulations.

3. **Plan seasonal and backup operation.**  
   Use differential-temperature control to collect heat when collectors are hotter than storage. Retain backup heating capable of meeting the required service during low-sun periods or solar-system outages. Select freeze protection—such as a suitable antifreeze loop or properly engineered drainback—using local minimum temperatures. Address summer overheating and low-demand periods through compatible stagnation protection and controls. Establish a code-compliant hygiene-temperature strategy alongside anti-scald mixing; solar preheating alone must not compromise microbial control. Compare backup fuels and operating schedules once tariffs and available utilities are known.

4. **Review installation and maintenance risks.**  
   Have qualified professionals verify roof strength, wind resistance, waterproofing, safe access and fall protection. Check pipe supports, thermal expansion, pressure ratings, corrosion compatibility and protection against leakage and contamination. Assess scaling risk from water quality and heat loss from long distribution routes. Provide accessible valves, pumps, strainers, sensors and storage components. Specify manufacturer- and code-based inspections covering leaks, insulation, mounting, controls, relief devices, mixing valves, scaling and heat-transfer-fluid condition where applicable.

5. **Commission and verify performance.**  
   Test pressure integrity, circulation, controls, freeze/overheat protection, backup operation, delivery temperatures and safety devices. Meter hot-water volume, relevant temperatures, solar heat delivered, backup energy and pump electricity. Compare performance with a documented design model using actual weather and demand, accounting for storage and distribution losses. Investigate persistent shortfalls or excessive backup use. Estimate savings and payback only after measured performance, tariffs and installed quotations are available."}
